acceptance: TestClockContract/system/stop_before_the_delay_prevents_the_run passes 200 runs in a row with -race under a CPU-loaded host (for example with GOMAXPROCS=2 and a busy loop beside it).
The fix keeps the contract the test states (a Stop before the delay prevents the run) and does not widen the delay so far that the case stops proving it.
A red-first reproduction shows the false return of Stop under load before the fix.
fix: Make the system-clock case of the clock contract deterministic under load: arm the timer with a delay the scheduler cannot reach before Stop, or assert the contract through the clock's own seam rather than wall time.
summary: TestClockContract/system/stop_before_the_delay_prevents_the_run failed once in the Go 1.27 ubuntu job of PR #1691 with clock_contract_test.go:173: Stop of a pending timer returned false. The same test passed in the same job of PR #1690 and passes locally on main and on both branches. PR #1691 does not touch internal/orchestrator. A flaky required test turns a correct PR red and costs a full CI rerun.
title: The system-clock stop-before-delay case of the clock contract test is flaky under CI load
